title: Southern Liang
capsule: The Southern Liang (南涼) was a Xianbei state of the Sixteen Kingdoms era in northwest China, founded in 397 when the Tufa chieftain Tufa Wugu broke from Later Liang allegiance and proclaimed himself a king based in the Hexi Corridor around modern Xining and Ledu. Ruled successively by Tufa Wugu, Tufa Lilugu, and Tufa Rutan, the kingdom fought recurring wars with its Xianbei and Xiongnu neighbors, including Western Qin and Northern Liang. It was extinguished in 414 when its last king, Tufa Rutan, surrendered to Western Qin's ruler Qifu Chipan.
